property_summary: For any non-zero address, the current owner of C can always successfully transfer ownership to it and c.owner() then returns that address; the mutant returns the zero address from owner(), so the onlyOwner check always reverts and ownership can never be transferred.
For any caller, a freshly deployed C's owner() getter returns the actual deployer (non-zero) rather than the zero address; the mutant always returns address(0), breaking this for every input.

The current owner can always successfully call renounceOwnership(), after which ownership is relinquished; the mutant's owner() always returns address(0), so the onlyOwner check fails and renounceOwnership reverts for every input.

The contract deployer is the owner, so the owner can always successfully call setCaller(fuzzerActor) to install that actor as cfo (succeeds in P for every non-zero actor); the mutant's owner() always returns address(0), so the onlyOwner check fails and setCaller reverts for every input.

For any non-zero address, the contract's owner() getter returns the deployer (non-zero) and an ownership transfer to that address succeeds and is reflected by owner(); the mutant always returns address(0) so the onlyOwner transfer reverts, breaking the invariant.

For every caller address, c.owner() must return the contract's fixed deployer/owner (the test contract), never the caller; the mutant makes owner() return the caller's address, violating this for any caller different from the owner.

After the owner renounces ownership, no address whatsoever can perform owner-only actions (setCaller always reverts); the mutant makes owner() return the caller, so any caller still succeeds after renounce.

After transferOwnership(newOwner) from the deployer, c.owner() must equal newOwner when observed from any address; the mutant returns the caller's address instead of the stored owner, so a call from an address other than newOwner returns the wrong value.

After the owner transfers ownership to a new address, the previous owner must lose all owner-only privileges (setCaller reverts for them); the mutant makes owner() return the caller, so the previous owner can still perform owner-only actions.

Only the stored owner may call c.transferOwnership: for any fuzzed caller other than the deployer the call must revert in P, but the mutant's owner() returns the caller itself, so _checkOwner passes and the call succeeds for anyone.

After the current owner calls transferOwnership(newOwner) with newOwner != address(0), the contract's owner() must equal newOwner for every input; the mutant transfers ownership to address(0), so owner() returns zero and violates the rule.

After the current owner calls transferOwnership(newOwner) with newOwner != address(0), the newly appointed owner must retain full ownership powers — specifically they can again call transferOwnership to hand over to another address — a property the reference satisfies for every input but the mutant breaks because it sets owner() to address(0), making the follow-up transferOwnership revert.
